method: Atlas territorial versions; >=55% of each new location inside the old territory polygon, with sourced corrections

active.reason: Desde 1569 se muestra el Gran Ducado de Toscana.
Título granducal concedido a Cosme I en 1569.
El ducado de Ferrara fue devuelto a los Estados Pontificios en 1598.
El ducado fue integrado en los Estados Pontificios en 1631.
El ducado separado de Parma y Piacenza se creó en 1545; los gobiernos anteriores requieren sus propias jurisdicciones.
El marquesado pasó formalmente a Saboya por el tratado de Lyon de 1601; su ocupación desde 1588 requiere otra capa.

territories.name: Austria
territories.note: Ducado/archiducado danubiano: no equivale al conjunto de posesiones de la Casa de Austria.

territories.name: Austria Interior
territories.note: Estiria, Carintia, Carniola y litoral habsbúrgico. Pitten y Wiener Neustadt seguían la rama estiria aunque hoy estén en Baja Austria.

territories.name: Tirol
territories.note: Condado del Tirol. Se excluyen los obispados de Brixen y Trento; Kufstein y Kitzbühel entran en 1504 y Lienz en 1500.

territories.name: Baviera

active.reason: Antes de la reunificación de 1505 había ducados bávaros de distintas ramas; esta capa solo muestra el núcleo reunido.

territories.note: Núcleo reunificado en 1505. Las ciudades imperiales, obispados y Pfalz-Neuburg conservan jurisdicción separada; la Alta Palatinado se incorpora en 1628.

territories.name: Palatinado
territories.note: Palatinado electoral, no todas las ramas Wittelsbach. La Alta Palatinado se transfiere a Baviera en 1628.

territories.name: Bohemia
territories.note: Tierras de la Corona de Bohemia: incluye Moravia y partes de Silesia, además del reino estricto.

territories.name: Hungría

active.reason: Después de Mohács (1526), título y control se disputaron; no se debe proyectar el reino medieval completo sobre la Hungría real, Transilvania y el dominio otomano.

territories.note: Corona compuesta de San Esteban antes de Mohács: incluye Croacia y Transilvania. Desde 1526 la partición queda sin colorear hasta modelar cada sucesor.

territories.name: Principado episcopal de Brixen
territories.note: Solo los núcleos Brixen y Bruneck están identificados; el dominio temporal completo del obispo tenía jurisdicciones superpuestas y aún no está dibujado.

territories.name: Principado episcopal de Trento
territories.note: Solo Trento y Cavalese/Fiemme están identificados. La autonomía de Fiemme dentro del principado y sus límites requieren una capa más fina.

territories.name: Arzobispado principesco de Salzburgo
territories.note: Solo núcleos comprobados, incluido el enclave de Mühldorf; no equivale a toda la diócesis ni a una frontera cerrada del Estado eclesiástico.

territories.name: Corona de Polonia

active.reason: La frontera de este corredor se ha auditado hasta la Unión de Lublin de 1569; conflictos y cambios posteriores quedan por fechar.

territories.note: Corona, no todos los dominios de los Jagellón. Mazovia se incorpora por etapas; los voivodatos transferidos desde Lituania se muestran desde 1569. Moldavia y Pomerania occidental no se absorben por vasallaje o proximidad.

territories.name: Ducado de Mazovia

active.reason: El último ducado mazoviano fue incorporado a la Corona en 1526; Rawa y Płock habían pasado antes.

territories.note: Ducado vasallo pero políticamente distinto. Rawa sale en 1462, Płock en 1495 y el núcleo restante en 1526.

territories.name: Prusia Real

active.reason: La Prusia Real se integró en la Corona en 1466; ocupaciones posteriores a 1569 quedan por fechar en este corredor.

territories.note: Provincia de la Corona desde 1466, distinta de Prusia ducal. Warmia conserva su condición eclesiástica dentro de esta agrupación cartográfica.

territories.name: Prusia de la Orden

active.reason: El estado de la Orden Teutónica fue secularizado como Ducado de Prusia en 1525.

territories.note: Remanente de la Orden tras la Segunda Paz de Toruń; su sujeción feudal a Polonia no equivale a incorporación.

territories.name: Prusia ducal

active.reason: Ducado separado y feudo polaco desde 1525; cambios posteriores a 1569 quedan por auditar.

territories.note: Sucesor secularizado del Estado de la Orden desde 1525, feudo polaco; la propia entidad mantiene color separado.

territories.name: Gran Ducado de Lituania

active.reason: La frontera de este corredor se ha auditado hasta la Unión de Lublin de 1569; los cambios posteriores quedan por fechar.

territories.note: Núcleo occidental y voivodatos cuya transferencia de 1569 se ha revisado. La frontera oriental y el litoral del mar Negro quedan deliberadamente grises hasta una auditoría fechada.

territories.name: Francia

active.reason: Antes de 1453 las ocupaciones de la Guerra de los Cien Años necesitan capas fechadas locales; el agregado queda gris.

territories.note: Agregado francés conservador desde 1453: Bretaña entra en 1532, Provenza en 1486 y el ducado de Borgoña en 1477. Los feudos y ocupaciones discutidos se revisan por separado; antes de 1453 el gris no significa ausencia de Corona francesa.

territories.name: Bretaña

active.reason: El ducado se unió a la Corona francesa en 1532; el matrimonio dinástico anterior no lo borró.

territories.note: Ducado separado hasta la unión formal de 1532. Incluye los seis polígonos bretones antiguos, no solo los tres de la ficha anterior.

territories.name: Provenza

active.reason: La unión formal del condado de Provenza a la Corona francesa está documentada en las letras de octubre de 1486.

territories.note: Núcleo provenzal de Aix, Draguignan y Digne. No usa Avignon, bajo el Papado, ni Nice o Barcelonnette, cedidos a Saboya en 1388. Se incorpora a Francia desde 1486.

territories.name: Inglaterra
territories.note: Reino inglés, con Gales bajo su Corona en esta escala; Escocia permanece separada incluso después de la unión personal de 1603. Calais y los núcleos de Guyena se registran aparte.

territories.name: Escocia
territories.note: Reino separado de Inglaterra durante todo este ensayo (1400–1650), incluso cuando comparten soberano desde 1603. Se corrigen las adscripciones erróneas del agregado antiguo: Man y las Feroe nunca se pintan como Escocia; Orkney y Shetland entran en 1469 y Berwick solo se muestra entre 1461 y 1481.

territories.name: Plaza inglesa de Calais

active.reason: Calais y su marcha permanecieron en manos inglesas hasta comienzos de 1558.

territories.note: Solo Calais, no todo Artois ni toda la costa del canal. La plaza pasó a Francia a comienzos de 1558.

territories.name: Plazas inglesas de Guyena

active.reason: Solo se muestran los núcleos documentados; la situación de Burdeos cambió en 1451–1453 y no se generaliza a toda Guyena.

territories.note: Núcleos urbanos documentados, no una reconstrucción completa de Gasconia ni de las ocupaciones de la Guerra de los Cien Años.

territories.name: Núcleo inglés en Irlanda
territories.note: Solo nueve locations urbanas y próximas a los núcleos de Dublin, Meath, Kildare y Louth. No equivale a una frontera cerrada ni al control efectivo de toda Irlanda; su extensión variable y la expansión Tudor quedan por fechar.

territories.name: Señorío de Man

active.reason: El señorío de los Stanley se estableció por concesión inglesa en 1406; la jurisdicción insular era distinta de Inglaterra y Escocia.

territories.note: La isla conserva una jurisdicción señorial propia bajo los Stanley desde 1406. Su vínculo feudal con la Corona inglesa no la convierte en parte del reino inglés.

territories.name: Bailiazgo de Jersey
territories.note: Jersey mantuvo su vínculo separado con la Corona inglesa desde 1204. Durante la ocupación francesa de 1461–1467 se muestra bajo Francia y reaparece como bailiazgo a partir de 1468.

overrides.reason: Gibraltar passed to Castile in 1462, not throughout the old Cádiz polygon's span.
Keep the Nasrid frontier at Gibraltar until the Castilian capture in 1462.
Antequera fell to Castile in 1410, before the old Málaga polygon's transfer.
Antequera passed to Castile in 1410.
Ronda fell to Castile in 1485, before the old Málaga polygon's transfer.
Castilian conquest of Ronda in 1485.
Loja fell to Castile in 1486, before the old Granada polygon's transfer.
Castilian conquest of Loja in 1486.
Charles V granted Malta to the Order of St John in 1530.
Benevento was a papal enclave within the kingdom of Naples.
Benevento remained a papal enclave within the kingdom of Naples.
Biella had passed to Savoy before this corridor starts.
Biella belonged to the Savoyard sphere during this series.
Milan ceded Vercelli to Savoy in 1427.
Vercelli passed to Savoy from Milan in 1427.
The Ferrara devolution did not include Venetian Rovigo.
The 1484 peace transferred Rovigo/Polesine to Venice.
Rovigo returned to Venice after the League of Cambrai conflict.
Venice held Rovigo/Polesine following the 1484 peace.
Rovigo returned to Venetian control after the League of Cambrai war.
The coastal Istrian city of Pola entered Venetian rule in 1331; this does not paint the Habsburg inland peninsula.
Rovinj was among the Venetian coastal communities of Istria, distinct from the inland Habsburg territories.
Zadar was acquired by Venice in 1409. The EU V ID is Zadar; Zara on this map is elsewhere.
Conservative year-end assignment following the 1409–1420 Venetian reconquest of Dalmatian coastal towns.
Split submitted to Venice during the 1420 Adriatic campaign.
Brač was among the islands acquired in the 1420 Venetian Adriatic campaign.
Kotor/Cattaro submitted to Venice in 1419; shown from 1420 in this conservative annual layer.
Piombino was a separate Appiano/Ludovisi state, not part of Medici Tuscany.
Mirandola was not acquired by Modena until 1711.
Guastalla was a separate Gonzaga duchy during this series.
Venice acquired Zadar in 1409; the old Croatian polygon must not continue to paint it as Hungarian.
The Venetian Dalmatian campaign of 1420 removed Šibenik from this Hungarian-Croatian aggregate.
Trieste accepted Habsburg protection in 1382, before the Gorizia inheritance in 1500.
Fiume/Rijeka passed to the Habsburgs in 1466; the coarse Carniola polygon misses this port.
Rijeka/Fiume passed to the Habsburgs in 1466; the old Croatian polygon must not keep it under Hungary.
Lienz belonged to the separate Görz lordship until 1500 and then was attached to the County of Tyrol, not Inner Austria.
Maximilian attached Lienz and the western Gorizian lands to Tyrol after the 1500 inheritance.
The former Bavarian court of Kufstein passed to Tyrol after Maximilian's 1504 conquest.
Kitzbühel belonged to the Bavarian courts transferred to Tyrol in 1504.
Brixen was a separate prince-bishopric; its city was not the secular county of Tyrol.
Bruneck was listed among the Brixen prince-bishopric's cities.
The Fiemme/Cavalese area belonged to the prince-bishopric of Trento, not directly to the secular County of Tyrol.
Freising belonged to the independent prince-bishopric.
The County of Werdenfels around Garmisch belonged to the Freising prince-bishopric.
Passau was a prince-bishopric distinct from the Bavarian duchy.
The imperial city of Regensburg was not incorporated into Bavaria in this period.
Mühldorf belonged to the Salzburg prince-archbishopric until the 19th century.
Laufen was a Salzburg city, not a town of the Bavarian duchy.
Pfalz-Neuburg was created as a separate Wittelsbach principality in the 1505 settlement.
The landgraviate of Leuchtenberg remained a separate immediate territory after the Upper Palatinate transferred to Bavaria.
Leuchtenberg was an immediate landgraviate, not the Electoral Palatinate.
Speyer was a free imperial city; a political alliance with the elector did not make it Palatine territory.
Landau was an imperial city pledged to the bishop of Speyer, then independent again; it was not Electoral Palatinate.
The counts of Leiningen had their own territory rather than forming a district of the Electoral Palatinate.
Pirmasens/Lemberg followed the counts of Zweibrücken-Bitsch and later Hanau-Lichtenberg, not the Electoral Palatinate.
The 1410 Palatine partition assigned Zweibrücken to a separate Wittelsbach line.
Sochaczew did not join the Crown with Rawa and Gostynin in 1462; its incorporation dates to 1476.
Sochaczew remained Mazovian until incorporation into the Crown in 1476.
The Tuchola/Schlochau area belonged to the Order before the Thirteen Years' War; its status during the war is left uncolored.
Pomerelia, including Tuchola, entered Royal Prussia after the Second Peace of Thorn.
The treaty explicitly assigned Malbork/Marienburg to the Polish Crown, not to the Teutonic remnant.
The treaty explicitly assigned Elbląg/Elbing to Royal Prussia.
The treaty includes Christburg/Dzierzgoń in the lands transferred to the Crown.
Malbork changed hands in the Thirteen Years' War and was definitively ceded to Royal Prussia in 1466; the contested years are left gray.
Elbląg changed hands during the Thirteen Years' War and passed to Royal Prussia in 1466; contested years are left gray.
Christburg/Dzierzgoń was transferred to the Crown in 1466; the wartime interval remains uncolored.
Malbork was Royal Prussia, not the secularized Duchy of Prussia.
Elbląg was Royal Prussia, not the secularized Duchy of Prussia.
Christburg/Dzierzgoń was on the Royal Prussian side of the 1466 border.
The Brixen city location represents an identified centre of the distinct prince-bishopric, not a complete diocesan boundary.
Bruneck is listed among the prince-bishopric's cities; only its location is attributed here.
The city was the seat of the prince-bishop; this location does not delimit the entire temporal principality.
Fiemme retained local self-government under the prince-bishop of Trento; the location is only an approximate geographic token.
Salzburg was a city of its distinct prince-archbishopric.
Hallein belonged to the territorial archbishopric, not the Duchy of Bavaria.
Mühldorf was a Salzburg enclave; its high-court jurisdiction is recorded from 1442, so this location should not be read as an unchanged bundle of rights.
Laufen was a Salzburg territorial town, distinct from Bavarian control.
The Calais town location marks the English-held port and Pale until its French capture in early 1558; the entire surrounding location set is not claimed.
Bordeaux was a centre of English Gascony; the 1451 French submission and the later English recapture require separate annual entries.
English forces regained Bordeaux in 1452, before the final French capture in October 1453.
Bayonne was part of the English-administered Gascon core before the French campaign of 1451; this is a city location, not all of Gascony.
The English held Calais until the French capture in 1558; the overlap with old Ponthieu must not transfer this location to France in 1477.
Barcelonnette and the Nice hinterland were ceded from Provence to Savoy in 1388.
The 1486 annexation of Provence did not restore Barcelonnette, ceded to Savoy in 1388.
Barcelonnette was among the Nice hinterland transferred to Savoy in 1388; the separate Savoyard layer records the location.
Tórshavn lies in the Faroes, under the Norwegian Crown within the Danish-Norwegian monarchy, not Scotland.
The Isle of Man had a distinct Stanley lordship from 1406 and is not a Scottish county.
The Man location denotes the Stanley lordship established in 1406, a jurisdiction distinct from the English and Scottish kingdoms.
Orkney remained under Norwegian rule until 1469; earlier years are left to a future Norway-Denmark layer.
Shetland passed from Norway to Scotland in 1469; earlier years are left to a future Norway-Denmark layer.
Berwick was held by England from 1333 until its transfer to Scotland in 1461.
England retook Berwick in 1482 and retained it thereafter.
Berwick was in English hands from 1333 until its transfer to Scotland in 1461.
England retook Berwick in 1482 and retained it thereafter.
Dublin remained the central English administrative town in Ireland; this location is a core point, not the Pale's complete outline.
Fingal is immediately north of Dublin within the English Pale core; this location is a cautious token, not a dated frontier.
Navan lies in Meath, one of the Pale's core counties; this is a location-level token, not a border claim.
Trim lies in Meath, in the core English-administered area; no complete Meath frontier is inferred.
Naas is a Kildare core location of the Pale; the extent of English power beyond it varied.
Kildare is shown as an English Pale core location, without implying county-wide effective control.
Athy is a Kildare garrison location in the English lordship; its location does not define the Pale's whole frontier.
Drogheda was a principal town in the Louth/Meath Pale area; this is an urban token, not a county-wide polygon.
Louth was one of the Pale counties; Dundalk marks its northern urban core without claiming a precise frontier.
The old Normandy polygon overlaps Jersey; the island was otherwise a separate bailiwick loyal to the English Crown, except for the occupation of 1461–1467.
Jersey retained a separate allegiance to the English Crown after 1204, before its seven-year French occupation.
The French occupied Jersey for seven years during the Wars of the Roses before it was recovered in 1468.
The English Crown recovered Jersey in 1468; the island kept its distinct bailiwick rather than becoming part of England.

audit.sourceCaveat: Geometric candidate coverage is not a historical border or ownership claim.
